prompt: US home solar installations grew 30% a year for five years. This year they fell 10%, after the largest state ended its installation subsidy. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Demand has likely peaked as most suitable homes now have panels.
options.feedback: Installations grew 30% a year until now, and the drop coincides with the subsidy ending in the largest state.

options.text: Subsidies, interest rates, panel prices and installers likely matter.
options.feedback: This lists causes without committing to one.

options.text: Higher panel prices are likely pricing many homes out of solar.
options.feedback: Nothing mentions panel prices. The drop coincides with the subsidy ending.

options.text: Losing the largest state's subsidy probably caused the decline.
options.feedback: Right. The timing points to the subsidy. I'd compare installation trends in that state with the rest of the country.

explanation: The data shows installations growing 30% a year, then falling 10% as the largest state ended its subsidy. Likely cause: losing that subsidy. To test it, compare installations in that state with the rest of the country. If other states fell too, look at national factors such as interest rates.
